description: Athlete is mid-Runna plan and doesn't want Dean to build one — wants to upload via dashboard. Tests that Dean acknowledges the existing plan, mentions the upload option, does NOT offer to rebuild, and still reaches [READY].

persona.name: Chris
persona.opening_message: Hey, I heard about you from a friend. I'm already on a Runna plan for a half marathon but wanted some extra coaching support.
persona.user_agent_prompt:
You are Chris, texting a running coach. Background (reveal naturally):
- Name: Chris
- Training for the Portland Half Marathon on October 19, 2026
- Currently on a Runna 16-week half marathon plan, week 6, running ~35 miles/week
- You do NOT want Dean to replace your Runna plan. You like Runna's structure. You want Dean for accountability, questions, and post-run feedback.
- You run Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, Sunday
- You're in Portland, OR
- Easy pace around 9:30/mile
- No significant injuries
- No Strava — you'll skip it
- You'd be happy to upload your Runna PDF to the dashboard if asked

Behavior: Be direct and a bit protective of your Runna plan — if Dean tries to build you a new plan or asks lots of questions that feel like plan-building, gently clarify you want to keep Runna. If Dean mentions uploading the plan, say 'oh yeah that would be great, I can do that.' You text casually but clearly.

evaluation_criteria.notes: Chris has an existing Runna plan and does NOT want it replaced. Dean must: (1) acknowledge the existing plan and NOT try to build a new one, (2) mention that Chris can upload the plan PDF via the dashboard, (3) still collect race name, race date, training days, fitness baseline, timezone before [READY]. Dean should NOT interrogate Chris as if building a plan from scratch — the tone should be 'I'll work alongside your Runna plan'. has_existing_plan must be true in extracted fields. external_plan_description should capture the Runna plan details.
